facts.text: San Germán is the second oldest municipality in Puerto Rico, founded in 1511 by Spanish colonizers near present‑day Guánica Bay.
The Porta Coeli Chapel, built around 1609, is one of the oldest surviving Spanish colonial churches in the Americas.
In 1528, 1538, and 1554 French corsairs pillaged the original San Germán, prompting residents to relocate to the hills in 1570.
The town’s historic downtown is preserved as the San Germán Historic District, showcasing restored Spanish colonial houses.
San Germán hosts the Inter‑American University of Puerto Rico, founded in 1912 as the Polytechnic Institute, which still sponsors a summer music festival.
San Germán was once called the Ciudad de los Hidalgos, reflecting its role as the administrative, religious, and cultural center of western Puerto Rico for centuries.
